A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Augmentation research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR10/100 and sentence-embedding experiments, including performance comparisons, freezing ablations, training trajectories, and representation analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds ImageNet100, graph-learning, PCA-augmentation, and supervised-learning results, including additional appendix analyses.

M1.justification: V2 introduces PCA-based augmentation as an alternative to dropout, subtracting a selected principal component from centered batch representations. It also adapts PCA to pooled node embeddings for graphs. Dropout, optional stop-gradient, partial-batch augmentation, and CKA-guided layer selection already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet100 image evaluation and graph classification on COLLAB, IMDB-Multi, NCI1, and PROTEINS, extending coverage to social and molecular/protein graphs. The earlier CIFAR, cross-CIFAR transfer, and seven STS benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds GCL as an evaluated graph comparator and standard supervised controls labeled Regular or No Dropout. SimCLR and SimCSE remain central. The detailed seven-task STS comparison is narrowed, including removal of the default SimCSE+MLM row, although MLM comparisons remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: V2 adds supervised-only training protocols, including 100 CIFAR epochs, and graph pretraining for 1000 epochs with validation/test separation and specified augmentations. It adds CIFAR dropout sweeps over 0.5, 0.25, and 0.125 and compute/memory estimation. The existing CIFAR batch size of 1024 and 1500 pretraining epochs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses compare dropout with PCA, largest versus sixth principal components, supervised versus contrastive learning, and Deep Augmentation with MLM alone. V2 also adds principal-value spectra, CIFAR dropout sensitivity, and graph layer/stop-gradient ablations. Earlier freezing, transfer, training-trajectory, and CKA analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: V1 provides no explicit uncertainty estimates or repeated-run counts. V2 Appendix C and Table 5 introduce standard deviations for graph comparisons. Run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unspecified; an increase in repeated runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: V2 adds PCA, supervised, graph, tuned-CIFAR, and compute results. New ImageNet100 scores are 79.38 for SimCLR and 79.56 with Deep Augmentation. The retained STS averages remain 75.86 versus 76.72. Five variant rows lose their full STS breakdowns from v1 Figure 8, although some averages survive in prose.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a mathematical definition of the batch-dependent PCA augmentation, including principal-component ordering and centering. The original InfoNCE and layer-composition formulations are essentially retained, with similarity clarified as cosine similarity. No new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion broaden the contribution from dropout-based augmentation in vision/NLP to PCA and graph learning. They add the central qualification that supervised learning exhibits adverse effects. CKA-based layer selection is promoted into the explicit contributions but was already described in v1.

C2.justification: V2 develops the earlier co-adaptation account into an information-collapse interpretation. It hypothesizes that preventing collapse helps contrastive learning but can harm supervised learning, where compression may be beneficial. It also interprets Deep Augmentation as counteracting MLM-induced non-uniformity, adding substantive explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the million-sentence Wikipedia training sample and 28-epoch CIFAR fine-tuning duration, and adds a PyGCL code link and graph augmentation parameters, including walk length and perturbation probabilities. Existing SupContrast and SimCSE code links and their earlier training details are retained.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands positioning around stop-gradient, dimensional collapse, and information bottlenecks, including a detailed comparison with Chen and He and new discussions of Jing, Tian, Shwartz-Ziv and LeCun, and Tishby and Zaslavsky. Graph-learning, PCA, and dropout-survey references accompany this broader framing.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, and discussion. It replaces Key Ideas with Main Results, organizes experiments as Ablations, puts sentence embeddings before vision, and moves architecture/freezing material into the appendix. The title and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 adds PCA, supervised, and graph panels plus summary and uncertainty tables. The STS display becomes a reduced Table 1 with a compute column, and the ResNet configuration moves from Figure 2 to appendix Table 4. Retained plots and heatmaps are resized and relocated within a different page layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence about the method's generality and boundaries: PCA comparisons test whether benefits are dropout-specific, graph/ImageNet experiments examine wider applicability, and supervised controls reveal failures absent from v1. Most earlier ablations remain. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed STS rows, although heterogeneous graph outcomes, unspecified run counts, and approximate compute estimates limit the strength of some claims.
